title: Lost in the Medina Pumpkin and Bean Tagine
subtitle: with Mint Couscous and Vegan Feta
description: It’s plant power all the way with our super-tasty vegan dishes! Our meat-free, dairy-free, honey-free dishes are amped with plant-based proteins, fresh produce, nuts and seeds. Best of all, they’re for everyone, whether you're vegan, vegetarian or flexitarian.

steps.text: Roast pumpkin: Preheat the oven to 220C, fan-forced. Line an oven tray with baking paper. Peel the pumpkin and cut into 2cm chunks. Put the pumpkin on the lined tray, drizzle with 2 tsp olive oil, season with salt and pepper and toss to coat. Roast for 20 mins or until tender.
Prep ingredients: Meanwhile, pick half the mint leaves, then finely chop the remaining leaves, discarding the stems. Crush or finely chop 1 garlic clove. Drain and rinse the beans.

Cook tagine: Heat 3 tsp olive oil in a medium deep frypan over medium-high heat. Cook the garlic, stirring, for 1-2 mins until fragrant. Stir in the beans, tomatoes, chermoula seasoning (see Make it yours), 1 tbs tomato paste and 1 tsp sugar and bring to a simmer. Reduce the heat to medium-low, cover and cook, stirring occasionally, for 5 mins or until slightly thickened.

Soak couscous: While the tagine is cooking, put the couscous in a large heatproof bowl, add 1 tsp olive oil, pour over 200ml boiling water and cover with a plate. Stand for 5 mins or until the water is absorbed. Season with salt and pepper, then add the chopped mint and fluff the couscous with a fork.

Serve up: Gently stir the roasted pumpkin into the tagine and cook for 1-2 mins until warmed through. Taste, then season with salt and pepper. Divide the mint couscous and tagine among bowls. Scatter with the mint leaves and crumble over the vegan feta. Enjoy!

Make it yours: Our chermoula seasoning has a slight chilli kick. For those who prefer less heat, reduce the amount to taste. ~ If you have some green olives and/or slivered almonds on hand, scatter over the tagine before serving. Delish!
